thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: eu-west1-primary-gpu-pool saturation detected. queue_length > 12k, 95th latency > 2.5s, autoscaler failing. page: @oncall. rule: gpu_pool_saturation_high. link: https://monitoring.redwood/in/alerts/84532 :rotating_light:
Erin (oncall): ack. I'm on it. quick snapshot pls (cpu/gpu/util, queue growth)
Meera (runtime): copying recent metrics: queue growth to 12.6k over 8m, avg token latency 2.8s, error rate spike 6%. top model usage: gpt-large-v2 (40%), gpt-medium (28%).
Sam (infra): trying a manual scale — hitting quota on eu-west1 GPUs. GCP quota shows v100-gpu cores at limit. getting 403 quotaExceeded.
Sam (infra): kubectl logs autoscaler:
```
E0901 12:12:11  autoscaler.go:211] provisioning failed: quotaExceeded: requested 16 -> available 0
W0901 12:12:11  autoscaler.go:215] fallback attempt queued
```
Erin (oncall): ok that's the kicker. Autoscaler can't add nodes. We need spillover to another region and a short-term throttle to protect SLOs.
Jay (sre): recommend enabling cross-region-fanout override to route new requests to us-west1 and eu-central while infra sorts quota. This is low-risk; we have pre-warmed spare in us-west1.
Meera (runtime): we have policy flag: route: {priority: [eu-west1, us-west1, eu-central], overflow: true}. I can flip overflow to prefer fallback regions. Will do if infra authorizes.
Sam (infra): authorized. flipping routing override now.
Meera (runtime): executing command to flip fallback (internal API):
```
POST https://controlplane.redwood/v1/routing/overrides
{ "scope": "customer-facing", "overflow_preference": ["us-west1","eu-central"], "enabled": true }
```
Meera (runtime): response 200. Started gradual reroute for new sessions. Existing sessions pinned to eu-west1. :thumbsup:
Lee (support): seeing customer reports of slow responses and some 429s from managed accounts. Top affected: AcmeCorp (25% of recent 429s), BrightHealth (12%).
Priya (acctMgr): pinging Acme support lead and telling them we're on active mitigation; will offer periodic updates.
Sam (infra): parallel action: requesting emergency quota increase from GCP. Submitted request id rq-9987. ETA unknown. Also standing up ephemeral spot GPUs in eu-west1 from partner pool — might take ~7-10m.
deploy-bot: NOTE: Canary rollback for model gpt-large-v2 scheduled? No, rollback aborted due to high traffic.
Meera (runtime): to reduce load fast we can temporarily enforce per-customer rate-limits or reduce max tokens for best-effort tier. Suggest: reduce max_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 for free tier and throttle concurrent requests to 2 per API key.
Erin (oncall): do the throttles. We need to protect paid and enterprise customers first.
Meera (runtime): applying per-customer throttle policy:
```
PATCH https://controlplane.redwood/v1/quotas
{ "tier":"free", "max_concurrent":2, "max_tokens":2048 }
```
Meera (runtime): applied. Observability shows inbound QPS drop ~18% within 90s.
Jay (sre): starting health checks on fallback region pools. us-west1 pre-warmed nodes are green. initiating steady routing to 35% of new sessions.
Sam (infra): ephemeral spot GPUs in eu-west1 up: 8 x a100-80GB. Autoscaler rebalanced, queue drain rate improved.
Lee (support): customers getting intermittent degraded responses but overall service reachable. No data exfiltration or errors beyond throttles. tagging incident severity: Sev2 -> potential revenue impact but mitigated.
Priya (acctMgr): AcmeCorp confirmed they saw improvement after 12:40 UTC. Asking for RCA and timeline.
Erin (oncall): quick numbers: peak queue 12.9k, dropped to 2.1k after spillover+throttle+ephemeral nodes. 429s per minute peaked 420 -> now ~30. Latency 95p back to 1.1s. Good progress.
Meera (runtime): follow-up: we observed a model-level hot spot — gpt-large-v2 requests have long context windows causing KV cache pressure. Throttle on that model helped. Will propose model-specific rollout controls in postmortem.
Jay (sre): log excerpt showing routing change:
```
INFO 12:14:22 routing.go:72 overflow override enabled -> redistribute 35% new sessions to us-west1
INFO 12:16:01 routing.go:88 fallback health checks passed: us-west1=OK eu-central=OK
```
Sam (infra): GCP quota request still pending; partner pool will likely give us buffer for next 48h. Opening ticket to request long-term quota.
deploy-bot: DEPLOY NOTE: manual kernel patch rolled to runtime nodes to reduce memory pressure — rolled to 10% of nodes for safety.
Erin (oncall): summary for handoff: mitigation steps taken: 1) routing overflow override -> us-west1/eu-central (Meera) 2) temporary per-customer throttles & token limits (Meera) 3) ephemeral spot GPUs added in eu-west1 (Sam) 4) prewarmed fallback routing to us-west1 (Jay) 5) account outreach (Priya/Lee).
Erin (oncall): customer impact: AcmeCorp & BrightHealth hit increased 429s and higher latency for ~18m, recovered. No data loss.
Erin (oncall): post-incident action items (short list):
- expand GPU quotas in eu-west1 (infra)
- model-level circuit breakers and quota-by-model (runtime)
- improve autoscaler error handling for quotaExceeded (sre/infra)
- run a cross-region failover drill (oncall, runtime)
- update runbook with partner pool steps (sre)

Erin (oncall): handing off to Jay for overnight monitoring and RCA start. Jay, you're on-call for next shift.
Jay (sre): taking handoff. I'll begin RCA doc and capture exact timeline + metrics. tagging owners for action items.
Meera (runtime): adding a temporary dashboard with model heatmap + queue per-region. will attach to RCA.
Lee (support): I pushed a brief status note to status.redwood with incident timeline and affected customers list.
Priya (acctMgr): will follow up with Acme tech lead and set up a post-mortem meeting tomorrow.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to S3 at 12:45 UTC. auto-notify subscribers.
Erin (oncall): thanks team. closing active mitigation. Please continue async notes in #postmortems and link RCA to this thread.
Jay (sre): will create postmortem draft by EOD and include action owners.
Erin (oncall): handoff complete.
